Title: How could we make a rotating NAC a reality?

Messages.Author: firstco...@aol.com
Messages.Body:
And subject line = entire point of thread

How could we, as a community, cause the NAC to rotate to a different
city each year? Who has the authority to make this decision, and what
would they need demonstrated in order to be convinced?

(My suggestion would be to remove the NAC from GenCon, and replace it
with a non-regional Qualifier, supplemented by small 1 round
tournaments, casual games, and draft tournaments. These would all be
aimed at being short, fun, and easy for new players to get into, while
still drawing a good number of experienced players.)

There are many good reasons, I believe, to move the NAC around--seeing
the country, giving Canada and Mexico a chance, general crappiness of
Indianapolis...hey, that rhymes...I think we should brainstorm and
approach whoever is in charge.

Who's in charge? What are your goals with regards to V:TES play at
GenCon?

-- Brian
General Crappiness of Indianapolis

Actually, that's where I think you're making an assumption that's not
entirely valid. To me, GenCon is an extravaganza that's worth seeing in and
of itself. The NAC is great and Week of Nightmares is great but whether
they're worth going to for their sake alone is somewhat questionable.

I think one thing you're definitely not taking into account in your
calculations are people who haven't qualified. Such people may very well
travel to GenCon and try their luck with the Last Chance Qualifier and if
they don't make it, so what? There's this HUGE gamefest going on all
around them. But the whole notion loses quite a lot if you rotate the NAC
away from GenCon. You can schedule other VtES tournaments at GenCon, of
course. But from the perspective of the Continental Championship, the LCQ
loses a lot of participants it would otherwise have. And there may be more
tournaments, but none of them will be as good as the huge LCQ with the
opportunity to qualify for the huge NAC tournament.

That's what bugs me about this. GenCon is an attraction and the NAC is
an attraction. Split them, and both events lose something. Enough so
it not be worth bothering with either. I don't get a flying fuck about
Convention Fees. After spending money on plane flights and hotels,
convention fees, even a GenCon 4-day pass, don't amount to squat by
comparison.

Fred

re-focus the major con effort into soliciting new players, perhaps with a
Origins '05-style, rotating tournament schedule for newbies, or a Rapid
Thought format.

Other, elaborate discussions are in the now-poorly-named subject thread:

probably not change the number of attendees much, as there are as many who
would take advantage of a proximal location as there are people for whom it
would be inconvenient. My personal conflict is temporal; I'll never get the
week of GenCon free in the next five years, no matter what (as I
nauseatingly drone on about everytime this topic arises ;-). *Shrug* I
guess my point is, everyone has conflicts... So long as you don't hold the
NAC on Christmas Day in Alaska, things will work out...

leaving GenCon early and people losing interest in VtES given the less
important nature of the Shadow Twin tournament and wanting to do other
things, especially with the 8 AM start time of the tournaments were the

I'm not saying rotating NAC wouldn't be a superior option for some
people. I think some people, given their particular gaming proclivities,
budget, traveling, latitude for vacation, and so forth have reason to
prefer it the way it is. Others would prefer to change it in some way,
such as for the reasons you give above. I'm just trying to point out
that different populations have different interests here that are not
mutually compatible. They're not going to be resolvable by any other
means than, perhaps trading off from one year to the next or just by
some form of voting and whoever loses gets quashed or something. I
guess I'm just trying to raise peoples' awareness about that point.

Ug. Misconception. More often, its only 10 days of vacation in the first
year, with 15 being "awarded" after five years service with a single co, and
20 only coming after ten years. Of course, good negotiation skills can
accelerate that timetable significantly. They're not kidding when they say
USsers are work-aholics, but its not always by choice ;-)
BTW, a typical US work calendar only has 8 to 10 observed "bank",
national, and religious holidays total; Jan 1st, Good Friday, Memorial Day,
Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve and Christmas
Day being pretty static. The last one or two are either Martin Luther King
Day, the day after Thanksgiving, and/or a so-called "floating holiday"
(which is usually used to extend another long weekend). Regional weirdness

in the South) to the tune of one extra day, is also present.
